title: Claude
author: Muvmhead1
selftext: Not sure if this is the right group, or not. But I recently discovered Claude and have been trying to make my own games in the browser option. I know nothing about coding. When I try to make games though the graphics looks so terrible and the movement is weird all that. How do I fix this?

comments.author: SphinxWar
comments.body: Why don't you ask Claude this question?

replies.author: Muvmhead1
replies.body: I have it just still doesn’t look the best.

replies.author: SphinxWar
replies.body: Well, what did it tell you?

replies.author: Muvmhead1
replies.body: It says okay than I go back into it looks slightly better. But still not the best. Idk maybe I’m asking to much i like games with good graphics like how realistic Call of Duty looks with the guns and the faces and stuff that’s what I’m trying to do, but it’s just not even close

replies.author: zephyrion_drakon
replies.body: It will still take a lot of effort to get something that looks that detailed. Instead of asking it to do that, ask it "How could we achieve this look?" - it'll lay out a plan and give you more specifics than if you just ask it. They can't one-shot anything remotely close to a AAA game. You will have to do a lot of graphics work, model work, picking an engine, working with it on the code, building worlds, getting all the assets for the worlds, menus, sounds, etc. It's doable but there are a lot of details to think about!

replies.author: SphinxWar
replies.body: It said "okay" to a quesiton "hey Claude, what could we do better to make this look better, what would you suggest"?

replies.author: AvonMexicola
replies.body: Claude is horrible at image gen, so it needs the right tools and the right reference to work with. So I let Claude prompt my chatgpt in browser to generate reference images it then uses to make something in blender.

replies.author: Pied_Film10
replies.body: This guy gets it. Claude acts best as a middleman that explains processes or design to other tools. Don’t limit yourself just to Claude when creating games or you’ll hamper the end result. Ignore those one-shot prompt posts.

comments.author: ichivictus
comments.body: Through effort, iteration, experience? I recommend learning the basics outside of ai so you know how to communicate what you need.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
>When I try to make games though the graphics looks so terrible and the movement is weird all that.

You have to iterate and start using external tools. And learn how to prompt and be a project manager. You can't one-shot everything.

replies.author: Muvmhead1
replies.body: Gotcha gotcha thanks! I just started recently, but I have a bunch of games. I’ve been trying to do but need the polish the graphics right now because they’re really blocky.

replies.author: CodeWizardCS
replies.body: The whole process takes some practice and learning but it's fun. I'm not sure what my workflow would look like with web.

comments.author: HiddenMoney420
comments.body:
If you do not have the skills to code, you need to have other skills in order to direct an AI to code.

Clarity of thought and written word, the ability to elaborate on minutiae, and extreme attention-to-detail are just a few examples. 

Just pretend you're instructing a 3-year-old to make a meal.

replies.author: Muvmhead1
replies.body: Hahah I like that yeah I use chat gpt a lot as well to help and it does but only a little I’ll have to see what to ask

replies.author: Goonmize
replies.body: Try better promoting. Go to chat got and tell it your idea and what kind of movement you want. Then tell it to make a prompt for clause to follow. Then give Claude that prompt but don expect it to spit out AAA stuff. It can make you a solid foundation but you still gotta learn how to do other things it can’t do well

comments.author: Fincut
comments.body:
You are in the right place. I know nothing about coding either, and my game took a few hundred hours, so I know the frustration.

What helped me most:
1. Ask for a real 3D library like Three.js instead of plain canvas drawing. That alone makes a big visual difference.
2. Change one thing at a time. "The lighting is flat" works better than "make it look better".
3. Describe what you see, or paste a screenshot. The AI cannot see your result unless you show it.
4. Name a reference, for example a game or a photo, and say what you like about it.
5. For weird movement, ask for easing and a fixed timestep.

If you want to see what this can look like, this is my own game, built the same way (Three.js, no coding background, graphics made in Blender): https://wildstone-studios.com/?k=aigamedev2

Do you have a screenshot of yours? I would be happy to say what I would try first.

comments.author: Bitwizarding
comments.body:
Try making models with Tripo or Meshy. Or get them online somewhere. Claude usually makes things with primitive objects like boxes and spheres with basic materials.

You need to learn a lot about performance in order to make a game that looks good and runs at 60 fps. Like pasting 2000 trees that all use a million triangles might crush a gpu, so you need to learn about replacing models with billboards and LOD (Levels of Detail).

Textures can use a lot of gpu memory and draw calls so you need to learn about that. You can ask Claude to teach you and it is pretty good. It just cant see what you're seeing when you play your game, so you have to be good at describing issues you see. Like what exactly is wrong about the movement?
